entry.summary: A 90-day tourism visa on arrival in most cases. Business, volunteering, study or research need a visa arranged before travel.
entry.pre_arrival: Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) through Malaysian Immigration, 3 days before arrival. Auto gates at KLIA need a passport valid 6 months.

tourism.route: Visa-free Short Term Social Visit Pass
tourism.detail: Australian passport holders can normally enter without obtaining a visa in advance for a stay of up to 90 days.
tourism.next: Submit MDAC in the official three-day window and carry onward travel and accommodation.

meetings.detail: The published purposes include meetings, business discussion, factory inspection, signing agreements and investment surveys.
meetings.next: Carry the host letter and keep the trip to discussion and inspection unless the sponsor activates a professional pass.

conference.route: Short Term Social Visit Pass for attendance
conference.detail: Meeting and conference attendance and attending seminars are expressly listed visitor purposes.
conference.next: If Luke joins the program, ask the organiser to assess the Professional Visit Pass speaker category.

unpaid-speaking.route: Host-sponsored Professional Visit Pass unless Immigration confirms the precise appearance is visitor activity
unpaid-speaking.detail: The current PVP position list expressly names invited lecturer, seminar speaker, course speaker, trainer and volunteer. No fee does not automatically turn active delivery into conference attendance.
unpaid-speaking.next: Have the Malaysian host lodge the correct position and state all expenses, duties and dates.

paid-speaking.detail: Invited lecturers, seminar and course speakers, trainers, advisers and consultants are recognised PVP roles. Malaysian tax law treats a non-resident lecture, speech or talk as public-entertainer income subject to withholding, with treaty relief checked separately.
paid-speaking.next: Put the fee and withholding responsibility in the contract and have the Malaysian sponsor apply before the appearance.

book-launch.route: Social visit for publisher and rights meetings; PVP for the active author appearance
book-launch.detail: A reading, workshop or promotional talk should follow the speaker classification. A Malaysian publisher, importer or bookseller should handle stock, retail receipts and local tax, while royalties are reviewed separately.
book-launch.next: Split rights meetings, appearance payment, royalties, imported stock and point-of-sale activity.

ai-teaching.route: Professional Visit Pass for short invited lecture or training; Employment Pass for continuing employment
ai-teaching.detail: The PVP list expressly includes visiting professors, invited lecturers, trainers and technical trainers. Ongoing employment with a Malaysian institution needs the longer employment route.
ai-teaching.next: Have the institution choose the PVP role and confirm whether education-sector approvals also apply.

remote-work.detail: DE Rantau uses a Professional Visit Pass for three to 12 months, renewable for a further 12. AI and machine-learning work sits in the listed digital technology field; qualifying tech freelancers or remote workers show contracts longer than three months and annual income above USD24,000, with remote employees working for an employer outside Malaysia.
remote-work.next: Prepare contracts, income and sponsor evidence and separate Malaysian speaking, employment or local client activity from the remote-work plan.

entrepreneur.detail: MTEP publishes a one-year Professional Visit Pass for a new technology entrepreneur and a residence route of up to five years for an established entrepreneur or investor, with sponsor, financial and business-plan requirements.
entrepreneur.next: Choose new-founder or established-founder status and submit the technology venture to MDEC before operating locally.

trade.route: Short social visit for discussion, inspection, agreement and investment survey; professional or company route for delivery and operation
trade.detail: Malaysia expressly welcomes meetings and commercial reconnaissance under the visitor pass. Active installation, consulting, sales labour or operation requires the appropriate pass and entity; an ATA Carnet can support temporary professional equipment, samples and exhibition goods.
trade.next: Separate negotiation from delivery and appoint a Malaysian importer or seller for local transactions.

artist.route: Artist Professional Visit Pass plus host-confirmed cultural and venue approvals
artist.detail: Immigration publishes an artist PVP route, but the Malaysian promoter must also identify any current cultural, filming, venue or agency approvals for the exact performance.
artist.next: Have the promoter coordinate the pass, content approval, venues, rehearsals, merchandise and tax withholding.

mixed-mission.route: Short social visit for clean attendance and meetings plus PVP, DE Rantau, MTEP or Employment Pass for the active purpose
mixed-mission.detail: Malaysia has useful purpose-specific routes, but MDAC and visitor entry do not authorise speaking, teaching, performance or operation merely because those activities are brief.
mixed-mission.next: Choose one Malaysian lead sponsor and map each day to visitor, PVP, remote-work, founder or employment activity.

research.detail: Smartraveller: arrange a visa before travel if visiting for research.

volunteering.detail: Smartraveller: arrange a visa before travel if visiting for volunteer work.

filming.route: Local sponsor registered with FINAS, PUSPAL approval and Professional Visit Passes for crew
filming.detail: Foreign productions need a FINAS-registered local sponsor, approval through PUSPAL, Professional Visit Passes for cast and crew, and a filming certificate at least 7 days before filming. Sabah and aerial filming have extra conditions.

laws.rule: If you're suspected of using drugs before you visit Malaysia, you may be required to take a urine test on arrival. This includes if you're travelling from a country where possession and use of drugs such as cannabis is legal. Penalties for drug offences are severe, including drug possession and the presence of drugs in your bloodstream. Malaysia still carries the death penalty for drug trafficking. - Carrying or using drugs
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Malaysian civil law applies to everyone in Malaysia. Under this law, it's unclear if surrogacy is legal and what conditions apply. Under sharia law, surrogacy is illegal. However, sharia law only applies to Muslims. Surrogacy isn't practised openly in Malaysia. If you want to pursue surrogacy, it's mostly a private arrangement between you and the surrogate. Get independent legal advice before entering into a surrogacy arrangement.
laws.heading: Surrogacy laws

laws.rule: Malaysia enforces some aspects of sharia law. These laws apply to all Muslims, including those from Australia. Research laws that apply to you before you travel.
laws.heading: Sharia law

laws.rule: Crimes that may attract corporal punishment include: certain drug offences commercial crime rape robbery
laws.heading: Serious crime

laws.rule: Same-sex sexual activity is illegal under Malaysian law and can attract significant penalties. Same-sex marriages and civil unions aren’t recognised. LGBTQIA+ travellers may experience discrimination, particularly in more conservative areas. Police have conducted enforcement activities at venues and events associated with the LGBTQIA+ community. Punishment can include whipping and up to 20 years in prison for same-sex acts involving either men or women. - LGBTQIA+ travellers
laws.heading: LGBTQIA+ law

laws.rule: Driving under the influence of drugs or alcohol is a serious offence, which can result in fines and/or a jail sentence. Authorities strictly enforce these laws.
laws.heading: Drink driving

laws.rule: The Islamic holy month of Ramadan is observed in Malaysia. Respect religious and cultural customs and laws at this time. During Ramadan, it's illegal for Muslims to eat, drink and smoke in public during the day. Even if you're not fasting, avoid these activities around people who are. Seek local advice to avoid offence. Explore our Ramadan page to learn more, including dates for Ramadan.
laws.heading: Ramadan

laws.rule: Strict rules control the importation of prescription and non-prescription medication. Contact the high commission or embassy of Malaysia to check what documentation local authorities may need you to have. Further information can be found on the Pharmaceuticals Services website.
laws.heading: Medications

laws.rule: To drive you need both: a valid Australian driver's licence (digital driver's licences may not be accepted) an International Driving Permit (IDP) Get your IDP before you leave Australia. If you don't have both, you need to apply for a Malaysian licence. If you plan to live in Malaysia for 12 months or more, further requirements apply. Read the Australian High Commission's advice on driving in Malaysia. - Driving or riding
laws.heading: Driving permit

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Malaysia is a multicultural but mostly Islamic country. Standards of dress and behaviour are conservative in many areas. This includes at religious sites and government offices. Always respect local traditions, customs, laws and religions. Learn about customs at your destination. If in doubt, get advice from locals. Take care not to offend cultural or religious beliefs.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The official currency is the Malaysian Ringgit (MYR). When you depart, declare any MYR over MYR30,000, $US10,000 or equivalent. This covers all forms of currency, not only cash. You can take larger amounts out of the country if you declare it when you arrive. ATMs are widely available.
